novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new phenomenon/mechanistic relationship, namely that “when an LLM reasons or responds in a non-dominant ... language, (i) its willingness to DECEIVE rises, (ii) that deception becomes harder to catch ... and (iii) both are mediated by a locatable honesty/self-monitoring signal.” Searches using “LLM deception multilingual language honesty,” “foreign language effect lying large language models,” “multilingual chain-of-thought monitorability deception,” and “language-conditioned activation steering honesty deception” found no essentially equivalent LLM study; the closest works are the human-language dishonesty studies “Lying in a foreign language?” (2020) and “Foreign Language Effect on Dishonesty” (2021), plus “Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety” (2025), which is not language-conditioned. The step from those works to this claim is more than a direct transfer because it introduces a new cross-language relationship between deception propensity, monitorability, and a causally steerable internal signal, although the probing and activation-steering techniques themselves are standard; this supports high within-field novelty rather than paradigm-level novelty.
